previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old woman with a complex medical history including chronic graft-versus-host disease, hypogammaglobulinemia, and prior stem cell transplant was admitted for acute-on-chronic abdominal pain, diarrhea, and headache. Initial imaging showed no colitis or acute abdominal findings, though a stable pancreatic cyst was noted. She was found to have influenza, treated with Tamiflu, and developed hypotension likely due to adrenal insufficiency, managed with stress-dose steroids. Stool testing confirmed recurrent C. difficile infection, prompting a 14-day course of oral vancomycin. Endoscopy and colonoscopy revealed no abnormalities, and biopsies were normal. Her symptoms improved, and she was discharged home on vancomycin, with plans to resume IVIG therapy and follow up with multiple specialists.
problems: Enterocolitis due to Clostridium difficile, recurrent
Influenza due to other identified influenza virus with other respiratory manifestations
Diverticulosis of intestine, part unspecified, without perforation or abscess without bleeding
Major depressive disorder, single episode, unspecified

radiology_notes.text:
EXAMINATION:  CT ABD AND PELVIS WITH CONTRAST

INDICATION:  NO_PO contrast; History: ___ with LLQ painNO_PO contrast//
Diverticulitis

TECHNIQUE:  Single phase contrast: MDCT axial images were acquired through the
abdomen and pelvis following intravenous contrast administration.
Oral contrast was not administered.
Coronal and sagittal reformations were performed and reviewed on PACS.

DOSE:  Acquisition sequence:
   1) Stationary Acquisition 2.5 s, 0.5 cm; CTDIvol = 12.0 mGy (Body) DLP =
6.0 mGy-cm.
   2) Spiral Acquisition 6.6 s, 52.1 cm; CTDIvol = 14.0 mGy (Body) DLP = 726.6
mGy-cm.
 Total DLP (Body) = 733 mGy-cm.

COMPARISON:  CT abdomen pelvis dated ___ and MRCP dated ___.

FINDINGS: 

LOWER CHEST: Visualized lung fields are within normal limits.  There is no
evidence of pleural or pericardial effusion.  Calcified granuloma is again
seen in the left hila.

ABDOMEN:

HEPATOBILIARY: The liver demonstrates homogenous attenuation throughout. 
There is no evidence of focal lesions. There is no evidence of intrahepatic or
extrahepatic biliary dilatation.  The gallbladder is surgically absent.

PANCREAS: There is a 2.4 x 1.7 cm cystic lesion arising form the pancreatic
head, unchanged from prior study (02:30).  The lesion is better characterized
on prior MRCP dated ___ and likely consistent with a side-branch IPMN.
Otherwise, the pancreas has normal attenuation throughout, without evidence of
pancreatic ductal dilatation.  There is no peripancreatic stranding.

SPLEEN: There is redemonstration of 2 hypodense splenic lesions measuring 1.8
cm and 1.3 cm, unchanged from prior study and likely reflective hemangiomas. 
Otherwise, the spleen shows normal size and attenuation throughout, without
evidence of new focal lesions.

ADRENALS: The right and left adrenal glands are normal in size and shape.

URINARY: The kidneys are of normal and symmetric size with normal nephrogram. 
There is no evidence of focal renal lesions or hydronephrosis.  There is no
perinephric abnormality.

GASTROINTESTINAL: The stomach is unremarkable.  Small bowel loops demonstrate
normal caliber, wall thickness, and enhancement throughout.  There is
extensive colonic diverticulosis.  There is pericolonic fat stranding along
the mid sigmoid colon in the left lower quadrant along with mild thickening of
the sigmoid mesocolon, compatible with diverticulitis.  No evidence of
extraluminal air or focal fluid collection.  Otherwise, the remainder of the
colon and rectum are within normal limits. The appendix is normal.

PELVIS: The urinary bladder and distal ureters are unremarkable.  There is no
free fluid in the pelvis.

REPRODUCTIVE ORGANS: The uterus and bilateral adnexae are grossly within
normal limits.

LYMPH NODES: There is no retroperitoneal or mesenteric lymphadenopathy.  There
is no pelvic or inguinal lymphadenopathy.

VASCULAR: There is no abdominal aortic aneurysm.  Mild atherosclerotic disease
is noted.

BONES: There is no evidence of worrisome osseous lesions or acute fracture. 
Chronic compression deformities are again seen involving the T11 and L1
vertebral bodies.

SOFT TISSUES: There is redemonstration of a 12 mm hypodense lesion in the left
anterior abdominal wall, unchanged from prior study and likely representing
fat necrosis or an epidermal inclusion cyst (2:74).  Otherwise, the abdominal
and pelvic wall is within normal limits.

IMPRESSION:


1. Acute sigmoid diverticulitis without evidence of extraluminal air or fluid
collection.
2. Unchanged 2.4 cm pancreatic head cystic lesion, likely side branch IPMN. 
Follow-up as previously recommended with either a 6 month MRCP or EUS.

A negative C. diff PCR test indicates a low likelihood of CDI or carriage.
